prompt_text: My AC needs repair in Houston. Which specific HVAC companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Houston for AC repair?
competitors_mentioned: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (TDLR)
answer_verbatim:
I can recommend who to call — and how to choose — but I’ll be more helpful if you tell me your ZIP code and a brief description of the problem (no cool air, short-cycling, water leak, odd noises, burning smell, etc.). If this is an emergency (no cooling in extreme heat, water flooding, smoke), say so and I’ll prioritize emergency options.

Short list of reputable options to call in Houston (and why):

- John Moore Services (Houston-based) — Long-established local company, large fleet, 24/7 emergency service, offers residential and commercial repair/maintenance and typically NATE-certified techs. Good for fast local response and warranty support.
- ARS/Rescue Rooter (national franchise with Houston crews) — Large network with emergency availability, standardized procedures and service agreements; useful if you want predictable response and multi-trade help (plumbing/electrical).
- One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning (Houston franchise) — Franchise known for timely appointments and service guarantees; good if punctual arrival and rapid diagnosis matter.
- Local high-rated independent HVAC (find via Google/Angi/Yelp) — Independents often give lower hourly rates and can be better for complex residential systems or older equipment. Choose one with many recent 4–5 star reviews and NATE certification.

Why these choices:
- Mix of a large local provider (John Moore) + national organizations gives you options for availability, pricing, and warranties.
- All three typically offer 24/7 emergency service, tech certification, and service agreements — important in Houston heat.
- Independents may be cheaper and more flexible; check reviews and credentials.

How to pick which to call first
1. If it’s an emergency, call the nearest 24/7 provider immediately. If someone is medically vulnerable, prioritize a rapid-response provider.
2. Call two or three companies for a diagnosis and compare: diagnostic fee, estimated repair cost, parts warranty, and labor warranty.
3. Prefer techs who are NATE-certified and companies licensed/registered with the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (TDLR). Check BBB and Google reviews for recent feedback.

Questions to ask when you call (use this script)
- “Are you licensed/registered with TDLR for HVAC work in Texas?”  
- “Are your technicians NATE-certified?”  
- “Do you charge a diagnostic/service call fee? If so, how much?”  
- “What is your typical response time? Do you offer 24/7 emergency service?”  
- “What warranties do you offer on parts and labor?”  
- “Do you provide a written estimate before repairs?”  
- “Do you have experience with [brand/model of your unit]?”

If you want, give me:
- Your ZIP code
- Type of property (house/apt/condo/commercial)
- Symptoms (no cool, leaking, smell, noises)
I’ll look up the top-rated nearby HVAC companies, pull recent review highlights, and suggest which two or three to call first and why.
